summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain, found to be due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation with volume overload, leading to pulmonary edema and cardiorenal syndrome. She also presented with acute blood loss anemia, likely from recent severe epistaxis, on a background of chronic anemia from end-stage renal disease, requiring three units of packed red blood cells. Her kidney transplant function remained stable on imaging, and worsening creatinine improved with diuresis. A chronic right acetabular fracture was incidentally noted on CT and managed nonoperatively. Hypertension was managed with discontinuation of amlodipine and initiation of labetalol. Seizure prophylaxis with levetiracetam was continued, and medication adherence was reinforced. She improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary edema on repeat imaging, weight reduction from 86.7 kg to 78.1 kg, and stabilization of hemoglobin at 7.8 g/dL. She was discharged home with service on increased furosemide, labetalol, and a short-term opioid supply, with follow-up arranged in heart failure, nephrology, and orthopedic clinics.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation
Acute blood loss anemia on anemia of chronic disease
